# Eduardo Visconti

> AI engineer and full-stack developer in Tampa, FL. Builds LLM agents with
> iteration caps and human approval, and the apps people use them in.

## Current role

AI Developer at United Financial Resources (Bradenton, FL) since April 2026.
Built from scratch, and owns, the company's deed retrieval service, made to
replace a lookup that takes someone 10 to 30 minutes by hand: integrations for
70+ records-portal platforms, 840+ counties set up for automated search, 60
architecture decision records, and 7,500+ tests run inside the shipped image on
every pull request. An LLM agent capped by iterations diagnoses broken portals
and proposes fixes, and a person approves any change to a county's validation or
retrieval settings. Also leads the frontend of AI Hub, the company's internal
multi-agent chat platform, used by about 60 employees.

## Work

- Forja: his own product, built solo since March 2026. A training app for
  lifting, HYROX, functional work and running, offline-first, React Native and
  Expo on Supabase, 5,000+ tests. iOS beta on TestFlight, open to anyone with
  the link, and a live web app. https://app.forjahybrid.com
- Deed retrieval platform: private, no link. Described above.
- AI Hub: internal, no link. Frontend lead: the full interface redesign, a fix
  for a streaming race that lost agent replies, and the MCP server that lets
  its agents search for deeds.
- ConsciencIA: client work, live. A private journaling app where a psychology
  practice's patients get AI feedback on what they write, with entries
  encrypted at rest and consent given item by item.
- Sueli Repulho: client work. The website and course sales pages for a
  clinical psychologist, static Astro with a PHP lead form.

## Stack

Python, FastAPI, asyncio, pytest, Playwright, Vitest, PostgreSQL with row-level
security, TypeScript, React, React Native, Expo, Next.js, Docker, GitHub
Actions, LLM agents with tool calling, MCP, LiteLLM with self-hosted models.
